title: Accelerating Large Volume Electron Microscopy Through Sparse Sampling
content: Many important processes occur over vastly differing length scales, with critically important information stretching from the nanoscale to the macroscale. Volume electron microscopy (vEM) is a powerful tool for studying biological systems in three dimensions across precisely these length scales, forming a critical part of the information pipeline that aids understanding both subcellular and ultrastructural relationships within cells and tissues [1].
